name: Sushi Go!

source.title: Sushi Go! rules of play (2014), copy

setup.text: Shuffle all the cards. Put the rest of the deck facedown in the middle after dealing.
Choose a scorekeeper and get paper and a pencil.
Deal a hand to each player, held secretly.
Everyone starts together; no start player is named in the rules.

turn.summary: Everyone picks a card at once, reveals together, then passes their hand left.
steps: Choose 1 card from your hand and put it facedown in front of you.
When everyone has chosen, all reveal together.
Pass the rest of your hand facedown to the left and pick up the hand from your right.
Repeat until hands are empty, then score the round.
Chopsticks: if you have them in front of you, call 'Sushi Go!' and take a second card on a later turn. Put the chopsticks back in your hand before passing.
Wasabi: a nigiri chosen after a wasabi goes on that wasabi and triples in value.

round_end: Everyone announces scores and the scorekeeper records them.
Discard all cards faceup beside the draw pile, except puddings, which stay in front of you.
Deal new hands of the same size from the draw pile.
end: After the third round is scored, ignore any leftover cards and score puddings. The highest total wins.

scoring.text: Tempura: each set of 2 scores 5. A single is worth 0.
Sashimi: each set of 3 scores 10. One or two are worth 0.
Maki rolls: most icons scores 6, second most scores 3. Ties split the points, dropping any remainder.
Nigiri: squid 3, salmon 2, egg 1; triple if on a wasabi.
Wasabi and chopsticks score nothing by themselves.
Puddings, after round 3: most scores 6; fewest, including none, loses 6; ties split, dropping remainders.

tiebreak: The tied player with the most pudding cards wins.

missed.text: Each wasabi takes only one nigiri, and only a nigiri you take after the wasabi is out can go on it.
You may hold several chopsticks, but you can use only one per turn.
If players tie for most maki rolls, nobody gets the second-place 3 points.
Puddings are kept across rounds and scored once at the end.
In a 2-player game no one loses points for having the fewest puddings.
Passed-on chopsticks may be taken by another player once you put them back in your hand.

not_covered: The two-player dummy-hand variant and the pass-both-ways variant are not covered.
